An autoimmune disorder in which immune cells attack and destroy the exocrine glands that produce tears and saliva.

Sjögren's syndrome.e: After the Swedish ophthalmologist Henrik Sjögren (1899-1986), who first described it.

ss.sicca syndrome: An autoimmune disorder in which immune cells attack and destroy the exocrine glands that produce tears and saliva.

Sjostrom.e: Borrowed from Swedish Sjöström, from sjö (“sea”) + ström (“sea, current”).

Sjoblom.e: Borrowed from Swedish Sjöblom, an ornamental surname composed of the elements sjö (“sea”) + an archaic form of blomma (“flower”).

d.g: A stout whip, especially made of rhinoceros or hippopotamus hide.
d.x: He learnt that he was a slave, in spite of all the petty airs he might assume, a slave shackled to a yoke, to be scolded when he lagged, flogged when he rebelled with the sjambok of the modern driver, Threat of the Sack.

d.g: To whip with a sjambok; to horsewhip.

sjambok.e: From Afrikaans sjambok, from Dutch sjambok, from Javanese cambuk, and as borrowed in Malay: modern Indonesian and Malay, ultimately from Persian چابک (čâbok). Originally spelt in the colonial Dutch transliteration tscamboek. sjark.e: From Norwegian sjark, from Russian, from English shark.
